name: Say It in China — The 30-Scene Survival Phrasebook for Daily Life
cover: $HOME/Desktop/03-内容创作/10-核心书籍/03-30个真实场景/en/cover.jpg
desc: You are at a crowded counter, the clerk is waiting, and your sentence has to work now. Say It in China is built for those daily moments: buying breakfast, asking a driver to stop here, explaining a problem at a shop, checking a bill, and handling small misunderstandings before they grow. 30 practical scenes, each with four-layer dialogues: Chinese characters, pinyin with tones, a word-by-word breakdown, and natural English. From-the-Classroom boxes share what a teacher of 6,000+ students repeats every week, and Top-3-Mistakes sections flag the errors English speakers actually make under pressure. Includes a phrase finder for fast review. 159-page PDF.

name: A Bridge Made of Characters — What Teaching Chinese to 6,000 Students Taught Me About Language and the Mind
cover: $HOME/Desktop/03-内容创作/10-核心书籍/01-对外汉语教学智慧/en/cover.jpg
desc: What does a Chinese character do to the way a learner notices the world? After seven years and thousands of one-on-one lessons, Tony Sheng collected the moments ordinary lesson plans leave out: the pause before a learner understands a character, the cultural assumption hidden inside a sentence, the sudden shift when sound, image and idea connect. 22 true classroom essays about language, culture, memory and attention — honest about the scientific debates, grounded in real teaching stories. For Chinese learners, language teachers, and anyone curious about how a writing system becomes a bridge between minds. 251-page PDF.

name: Growing a Hundred Brains — How One Person Runs an Army of AI Agents
cover: $HOME/Desktop/03-内容创作/10-核心书籍/02-AI时代个人跃迁/en/cover.jpg
desc: Execution is no longer the scarce resource; judgment is. Growing a Hundred Brains is a first-person field notebook from the front line of working with AI agent fleets: how one person delegates drafting, research, testing and reporting to many small machine workers while keeping direction, taste and final decisions human. It introduces machine-time — a layer of productive time that runs beside your attention — and shows the hard parts honestly: what to delegate, how to write sharper instructions, how to check outputs and recover from failed runs. Practical language for agent orchestration and solo-team design. 209-page PDF.
